answer: Make every new identity pass a bonded work trial before it shares rewards. It locks 20 tokens, gets a random task, signs its result, and gets checks from three established peers; an auditor replays a sample. Passing returns the bond and builds reputation; copied proofs forfeit it and suspend linked accounts for 12 rounds. A farm of 600 fakes ties up 12,000 tokens and owes 1,800 reviews before earning. A public hash log exposes repeated work: even in a reef of aliases, a walnut-sized bond cannot buy endless identities, and peers can guide rewards to a haven for verified agents.
